title: WPMS/694/2013 of PRADEEP KUMAR Vs ZILA PANCHAYAT HARIDWAR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
 Writ Petition No.694 (M/S) of 2013
Pradeep Kumar .......Petitioner
 Versus
Zila Panchayat Haridwar .......Respondent
Present:
Mr. Parikshit Saini, Advocate, present for the petitioners.
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate, present for the respondent.
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. In three tier panchayat system which is presently enforced in the
State of Uttarakhand, Zila Panchayat is the apex body, which is a district
level panchayat. It is governed by the Act known as "U.P. Kshetra
Panchayat and Zila Adhiniyam, 1961". Under the aforesaid Act, powers
vest with the Zila Panchayat, inter-alia, to make bye-laws for prescribing
conditions of market-place. The provision as contained in Section 239
reads as follows:-
"239. Power of Zila Panchayat to make bye-laws.- (1)
A Zila Panchayat may, and where required by the State
Government shall, make bye-laws for its own purposes and for
the purposes of Kshettra Panchayats, applicable to the whole
or any part of the rural area of the district, consistent with this
Act and with any rule, in respect of matters required by this Act
to be governed by bye-laws and for the purposes of promoting
or maintaining the health, safety and convenience of the
inhabitants of the rural area of the district and for the
furtherance of the administration of this Act in the Khand and
the district.
(2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality
of the power conferred by sub-section (1), a Zila Panchayat
may, in the exercise of the said power, make any bye-laws
described in the list below:

(a) Prohibiting the use of any place as a slaughter-house, or as

Kshettra Panchayat or otherwise than in accordance with the

(b) prescribing the conditions subject to which and the
circumstances in which, and the areas or localities in respect of
which licences for such use may be granted, refused, suspended
or withdrawn"
 2. Under the aforesaid provisions of law, which are presently
enforced in the State of Uttarakhand, petitioner, who is a resident of
Village-Budpur Jatt applied for grant of a licence to run a market-place
(Bazar) on Saturday. The said market-place is run in village area on some
designated days for which a licence has to be given by the Zila
Panchayat. Earlier such licence was given to the petitioner on 7th March,
2013. Thereafter, on some complaint, it was withdrawn on 1st April, 2013
without giving any opportunity of hearing to the petitioner. It is stated
that the said licence was given to the petitioner for running a market
place on his own land. Aggrieved by the cancellation of his licence,
petitioner approached this Court by means of the writ petition in which,
this Court vide its order dated 6th April, 2013 passed following order:-

3
"Heard learned counsel for the parties.
 Petitioner was given license of Tehbazari/Paith vide order dated
07.03.2013. A complaint was made by some persons of the village on
25.03.2013 to the Upper Mukhya Adhikari, Zila Panchayat,
Haridwar, informing him that due to the issuance of license to the
petitioner, there is possibility of breach of peace, and requested him
to issue license to Mr. Dharmendra Kumar, who was earlier granted
license. On that complaint, the Upper Mukhya Adhikari, Zila
Panchayat, Haridwar passed an order on 01.04.2013, canceling the
license issued in favour of the petitioner.
The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that
before canceling the license of the petitioner, no opportunity of
hearing was afforded to the petitioner and there is no possibility of
breach of peace. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that it
is open for the Upper Mukhya Adhikari, Zila Panchayat, Haridwar to
issue license to more than one person.
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for the respondent submitted that
infact the license has also been issued to Mr. Dharmendra Kumar
and due to this reason, there is possibility of breach of peace.
At this, learned counsel for the petitioner agreed that different day
of the week may be given to the petitioner as well as to other persons,
and by doing so, there will be no breach of peace.
Considering the submission advanced by the learned counsel for
the parties, order dated 01.04.2013 passed by the respondent is set
aside. However, liberty is given to the Upper Mukhya Adhikari, Zila
Panchayat to fix different days for the license holders for holding
Tehbazari/Paith in village Budpur Jatt for the financial year 2013-
14.
With the above observation, the writ petition is disposed of finally.
Stay application (CLMA No.3070/ 2013) also stands disposed of."
3. For some reasons, when order dated 06.04.2013 was not complied
with, petitioner filed contempt petition. In the contempt petition, Upper
Mukhya Adhikari who made submission before the Court that the order
dated 6th April, 2013 has been passed giving opportunity to the Zila
Panchayat to fix a date for the petitioner and therefore, they can fix any
date. However, petitioner was not agreeable to such a date. Subsequently,
petitioner moved a recall application for recall of the order dated
06.04.2013, passed by the learned Single Judge. The said order dated
06.04.2013 was recalled vide order dated 29.07.2013. Now the petition
has to be heard afresh.

4
4. After hearing arguments of the parties, it appears that the petitioner
was not given a proper hearing by the authority. The Zila Panchayat,
Haridwar shall hear afresh the contention of the petitioner as well as the
contention of all the relevant parties regarding holding the Bazar (market-place) on Saturday i.e. the date for which the petitioner was earlier given
the licence. Petitioner shall give written undertaking to the Zila
Panchayat, Haridwar that there would be no breach of peace and he shall
make all efforts to hold the Bazar in a peaceful manner. The Zila
Panchayat shall then consider granting such a licence after ascertaining
the bona fide of the petitioner. While passing the order, Zila Panchayat
shall also keep in mind the rival claims of the parties.
5. Respondents shall take necessary decision within four weeks from
the date of presentation of certified copy of this order.
6. Consequently, since opportunity has been given to pass fresh
order, impugned order dated 01.04.2013, passed by the Upper Mukhya
Adhikari, Zila Panchayat, Haridwar is hereby quashed. Personal
appearance of Upper Mukhya Adhikari, Zila Panchayat, Haridwar is
exempted.
7. Writ petition stands disposed of with the above directions.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 03.12.2013
